title: China Steps Back From Promoting Second-Life EV Batteries
raw_summary: China spent much of the 2010s electrifying urban bus fleets while most countries were still testing whether battery-electric buses could replace diesel. By the end of 2025, it had 551,400 new-energy urban buses, representing 87.5% of the fleet. That early success has brought China to a stage other countries will encounter later, when large numbers of batteries reach the end of their automotive service and owners must decide what to do with them. In 2021, Chinese policy encouraged companies to give retired EV batteries a second life in stationary energy storage, backup power and charging infrastructure. The idea was attractive. A battery that had lost enough capacity to become less useful in a vehicle could still store substantial electricity, potentially avoiding the manufacture of another battery.
summary: China spent much of the 2010s electrifying urban bus fleets while most countries were still testing whether battery-electric buses could replace diesel. By the end of 2025, it had 551,400 new-energy urban buses, representing 87.5% of the fleet. That early success has brought China to a stage other countries will encounter later, when large numbers of batteries reach the end of their automotive service and owners must decide what to do with them.
article_paragraphs: China spent much of the 2010s electrifying urban bus fleets while most countries were still testing whether battery-electric buses could replace diesel. By the end of 2025, it had 551,400 new-energy urban buses, representing 87.5% of the fleet. That early success has brought China to a stage other countries will encounter later, when large numbers of batteries reach the end of their automotive service and owners must decide what to do with them.

In 2021, Chinese policy encouraged companies to give retired EV batteries a second life in stationary energy storage, backup power and charging infrastructure. The idea was attractive. A battery that had lost enough capacity to become less useful in a vehicle could still store substantial electricity, potentially avoiding the manufacture of another battery.

China has now changed its regulatory approach. New rules effective in April 2026 repealed the earlier cascade-utilization framework. A July 30 announcement from the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology withdrew special recognition for cascade-utilization companies and directed industry associations to discontinue promotional activities associated with the category.

Some reporting has described this as China banning second-life batteries. That misrepresents the change. Retired vehicle batteries can still be used in suitable applications when the resulting products meet the applicable standards. Reuse in electric bicycles and other restricted applications is prohibited. The ministry’s stated concern is the safety of inadequately tested, reassembled batteries with varying remaining capacity and inconsistent cell condition.

China’s experience deserves attention because battery retirement is becoming an industrial activity rather than a small collection of pilot projects. Electric buses have been operating for years, battery manufacturers have expanded production, and companies have invested heavily in recovering materials from retired packs. The assumptions that looked sensible when batteries were expensive and early electric fleets were young are now being tested against practical experience.

There is also an economic question beyond the regulatory change. New lithium iron phosphate batteries have become much cheaper, while old packs differ in age, condition, design and operating history. Testing, repackaging, controls and warranties can consume the savings from reusing cells. A second-life installation has to compete with new products designed for the same application.

That does not eliminate useful reuse opportunities. Operators with known battery histories and suitable stationary applications may have advantages that companies buying mixed retired packs do not. Product quality and economics will determine how much of the anticipated second-life market develops.

In my longer TFIE Strategy Briefing assessment , I examine how those conditions are changing, what China’s recycling industry reveals and why European policymakers and investors should reconsider assumptions about the supply of retired batteries. Subscribe for the deeper evidence and analysis.

article_paragraphs: CATL hit another milestone in its solid-state battery development, advancing to 20 Ah cells. The world’s leading battery maker aims to begin small-scale production in 2027.

CATL remains the leading global EV battery manufacturer by a wide margin. According to SNE Research , CATL held a commanding 39.9% share of the global EV battery market through the first half of 2026.

To stay ahead, the company is advancing several new battery chemistries, including solid-state and sodium-ion, promising to be safer, more efficient, and lower cost than traditional lithium-ion batteries.

When investors asked about the progress of its solid-state battery program on Tuesday, CATL said it continues to invest heavily in all-solid-state batteries and expects to begin small-scale production in 2027.
As it has stated before, output is expected to be limited at first as it scales up to mass production around 2030.
Speaking at the Summer Davos Forum in June, CATL chairman and CEO Robin Zeng said that, on a scale of one to nine, all-solid-state batteries have only reached level four.
All-solid-state batteries differ from semi-solid-state batteries in that they require a solid electrolyte to conduct lithium ions, rather than a liquid.
The company uses a sulfide-based solid electrolyte system, which offers high ionic conductivity and deformability, but maintaining stable contact between solid components remains a hurdle.

Tesla quietly registered Tesla Motors Vietnam LLC in Ho Chi Minh City on September 11, with about 77.7 billion dong (roughly $3 million) in charter capital and a business scope covering car imports, wholesale, and retail. Tesla never commented on it.
Now we have the first confirmation from someone inside the company. Ricky Ip, who recruits for Tesla, posted on X this morning:

Tesla is officially coming to Vietnam – and we're hiring. It started hiring in the Philippines in September 2024 and launched in early 2025. So a Vietnam launch in the next few months wouldn’t be a surprise.

There’s no word yet on pricing, models, or store locations. Oddly, the recruiting graphic features the next-generation Roadster, with fine print saying the vehicle is “for illustration purposes only.” Fair enough.

Before the good exhaust showed up, though, I needed a pick-me-up. A little commiseration to make me feel better. So I asked about the dumbest decisions that previous owners had made with your cars , and we got some pretty wild answers. Let's take a look at a few of the most popular ones.

I don't buy modded cars. I don't want to have to figure out what problems the previous owner installed. BUT... In this case, I inherited one. After my Dad passed away, I inherited an old 'bull nose' SAAB 96. Those had a weird water pump/generator all-in-one device that would destroy the water pump end regularly. I suspect it was because of electrolysis from the generator effecting the wear of the water pump bearings (but I am guessing). Meanwhile, Dad couldn't find parts to fix it or find a shop to rebuild it. Being the king of Gerry Rigging that Dad was, he pulled apart an old washing machine and removed the belt driven water pump. He rigged up a few brackets, mounted it, and rerouted the V-belt to drive the washing machine pump. It wasn't pretty, but it worked. It was still working when I sold it on. I don't know if that was dumb or genius... there is a fine line in between sometimes.

Oh! My '01 Camaro. My car came from the factory with the Monsoon system but I assume someone stole the head unit and they replaced it with the cheapest stock head unit before I bought it. As I was installing the required Pioneer Stereo with the removable faceplate and the dolphin animations, I found a Fanta can behind the stereo which is what kept it from falling into the dash since it was shallower than the Monsoon unit.

Never seen anything like this before in all my years of car stereo-ing, but the previous owner of my S8 had connected a subwoofer amp to the car battery by cutting off the leads of a perfectly good set of jumper cables, clamping one end to the battery, and wiring the bare ends to the amp.

Bought a 'race prepped' Fox body with the intent of doing a cheap drag build and the owner told me that he was selling his dads project for him, needed it gone "now" had a professional install a bunch of stuff including a battery relocation, fuel cell and a 6 point cage.
It was a roller, no rust and the frame and body looked good and straight. Price was, in retrospect, a little too good but i snapped it up.

title: Ford casts 5,000 ‘unicastings’ for Fathom EV truck in Tesla-style shift
raw_summary: Ford has now produced more than 5,000 large aluminum “unicastings” for the Fathom, its upcoming $28,350 midsize electric pickup, as it fine-tunes the process ahead of a 2027 launch. Each truck gets two of them, front and rear, replacing 146 individual parts. It’s the clearest sign yet that Ford is all-in on the manufacturing approach Tesla popularized with its Giga Press six years ago.

article_paragraphs: Ford has now produced more than 5,000 large aluminum “unicastings” for the Fathom, its upcoming $28,350 midsize electric pickup, as it fine-tunes the process ahead of a 2027 launch.

Each truck gets two of them, front and rear, replacing 146 individual parts. It’s the clearest sign yet that Ford is all-in on the manufacturing approach Tesla popularized with its Giga Press six years ago.

The update comes from Vladimir Bogachuk, Ford’s chief engineer of advanced vehicle structure architecture, in a post on Ford’s From the Road blog . The castings are made at Ford’s Shelbyville Technical Center and shipped to Louisville Assembly Plant for process testing and prototype builds. Louisville is the Kentucky factory Ford is retooling for the Fathom and other vehicles on its Universal EV Platform .

Ford melts aluminum ingots at about 1,300°F (700°C) and injects the metal into either a front or rear structure mold. Once a robot pulls the part out, it goes into a quench tank, gets trimmed and machined, and then runs a gauntlet of checks: industrial X-ray scans for pores and voids, dimensional measurements in a climate-controlled room, optical surface scans, and lab tensile and chemistry tests on samples.
Nothing ships to Louisville until a batch clears every inspection. Ford says it’s also working on cutting cycle time and on designing the castings for “modular repairability.”

That last part has been the main reason why automakers have been reticent about larger cast parts. Repair cost is the biggest knock on giant castings, since a damaged one-piece structure can turn a moderate crash into a write-off. Lucid executive Cory Steuben has said insurance concerns drove the company’s decision to skip gigacasting altogether.

Tesla kicked this off in 2020 with the first IDRA Giga Press at Fremont, a machine with roughly 6,000 tons of clamping force. It cast the Model Y’s rear underbody in a single piece , replacing 70 parts, and Elon Musk said the change removed the need for about 300 robots.

Tesla wanted to go much further. It added a front casting, tied the two together with a structural battery pack, and moved to even bigger presses for the Cybertruck. But in 2024, Reuters reported that Tesla had backed away from its plan to cast nearly the entire underbody in one piece, and the automaker has reportedly since dropped the front casting on some Model Y production.

article_paragraphs: Most electric motorcycles have something in common: a single-speed transmission. But a British company is preparing to shake things up at this year’s EICMA motorcycle show in Milan, where it will unveil a new electric motorcycle demonstrator featuring an unusual two-speed transmission designed to shift gears without interrupting power delivery.

The company behind the technology, E-Motiv Shift Systems , has developed what it calls a seamless powershift transmission, promising improved acceleration, better efficiency, and a more engaging riding experience.
Unlike conventional motorcycle transmissions, which generally require a brief interruption in power during gear changes, E-Motiv’s system is designed to maintain torque throughout the shift.

That could offer some interesting advantages for electric motorcycles, where a lower first gear could provide stronger acceleration while a taller second gear could help optimize motor efficiency at higher speeds.

Of course, most electric motorcycles don’t actually need multiple gears, and very few have ever offered multi-speed transmissions . Electric motors produce strong torque across a wide operating range, which is why manufacturers generally prefer the simplicity, lower weight, and reduced maintenance of single-speed drivetrains.
E-Motiv’s technology actually traces its roots back nearly 25 years to the Zeroshift transmission system, which eventually found its way into Aprilia’s MotoGP racing motorcycles in 2015.

The latest electric version was developed through a £1 million UK government-funded project involving motorcycle manufacturer BSA, the University of Bath, and the Institute of Advanced Automotive Propulsion Systems (IAAPS).
The demonstrator motorcycle, known as Demo 1, was conceived by British design consultancy Envisage and is being built by IAAPS. Real-world testing is scheduled to begin in early 2027.

The RED is a European success story. It remarkably drove the deployment of renewables in the last decades. Not reopening the RED is the most rigorous and timely pathway to ensure regulatory stability and not amending the rules is the best simplification exercise.

The Renewable Energy Directive has been revised four times in as many years. While each revision addressed legitimate policy developments, the cumulative effect is that the new provisions included since 2023 are still yet to be implemented in most EU Member States.

This regulatory instability undermines the investment certainty essential to meeting Europe’s climate and energy security objectives. Investment in renewable energy and associated infrastructure depends on predictable regulatory frameworks. Financial institutions require clarity on targets, permitting procedures, grid and network access rules, auction mechanisms to underwrite long-term deployment and effective power purchase and heat purchase agreement frameworks.

raw_title: Tesla Semi catches fire on I-880 with no crash, closes freeway for 10 hours
title: Tesla Semi catches fire on I-880 with no crash, closes freeway for 10 hours
raw_summary: A Tesla Semi caught fire on Interstate 880 in Hayward, California, on Tuesday evening, and there was no crash. The electric truck’s lithium-ion battery burned long enough to keep the southbound freeway closed for about 10 hours. The driver got out unhurt. But a Class 8 electric truck catching fire on its own, in traffic, is something Tesla and its growing list of Semi customers need to explain.
summary: A Tesla Semi caught fire on Interstate 880 in Hayward, California, on Tuesday evening, and there was no crash. But a Class 8 electric truck catching fire on its own, in traffic, is something Tesla and its growing list of Semi customers need to explain.
article_paragraphs: A Tesla Semi caught fire on Interstate 880 in Hayward, California, on Tuesday evening, and there was no crash. The electric truck’s lithium-ion battery burned long enough to keep the southbound freeway closed for about 10 hours.
The driver got out unhurt. But a Class 8 electric truck catching fire on its own, in traffic, is something Tesla and its growing list of Semi customers need to explain.

The fire broke out at around 5:35 p.m. PT in the southbound lanes near Route 92. CHP Hayward then closed I-880 in both directions, citing “the potential risk of hazardous chemical smoke,” and posted these photos from the scene:

🚨 TRAFFIC ALERT – I-880 FULL CLOSURE 🚨 A Tesla semi-truck has caught fire on I-880, resulting in a complete shutdown of both northbound and southbound lanes due to the potential risk of hazardous chemical smoke. pic.twitter.com/O01z32nxpZ
The driver told officers the truck caught fire and that they didn’t know why. No other vehicles were involved.

Northbound reopened Tuesday night. Southbound took much longer. CHP initially warned that the battery could burn for 15 to 18 hours, but crews beat that estimate, and CHP Hayward posted that all lanes were open at around 3:30 a.m. Wednesday.

The CHP photos show firefighters laying foam around the burned-out tractor, with the front of a Premier Trailer Leasing trailer charred behind it. The truck’s operator hasn’t been identified, and Tesla, which doesn’t have a press office, hasn’t commented. The cause is under investigation.

We’ve been here before. In August 2024, a Tesla-operated Semi caught fire on I-80 near Emigrant Gap while driving from Livermore to Tesla’s facility in Sparks, Nevada. At the time, no crash was reported. The NTSB later found the truck had left the road on a curve, hit a delineator post and a tree, and its battery ignited after the impact. Firefighters used about 50,000 gallons of water, and the lanes stayed closed for up to 15 hours.

While it's just one number off from being half of 666, the 2002 Volkswagen GTI 337 (named for the internal VW code for the original GTI) we looked at on Tuesday didn't come close to being half bad. Unfortunately for its seller, however, few of you found anything good in its $13,337 price tag. When all was said and done, that fell in an 80% 'No Dice' loss

When the Ford Motor Company introduced the Mustang on April 17 th , 1964, it didn't just create an instant hit that defined a new category and became the marque's brand ambassador for decades to come. With that launch, the company also set the stage for a cottage industry of Mustang modifiers. Obviously, the best-known is Carroll Shelby, whose namesake GT-Number models turned Ford's pony from secretary specials into real race cars. Others, including Steve Saleen, Steeda Autosports, and racing legend Jack Roush, have put their mark on the Mustang over the years.

According to its ad, this 2012 Ford Mustang GT is one of 105 Roush Stage 2 cars built for that model year. The Stage 2 mods include visual changes: rocker stripes, a white-and-gray hood appliqué, louvers over the side lights, front and rear spoilers, and RS2 (Roush Stage 2) badging. The interior features white-faced gauges and Jack Roush signature embroidery on the bucket seat backs.

The Roush riot doesn't stop at the aesthetics, either. Underneath, the car has been massaged with stiffer springs and revised suspension geometry for tauter handling. Putting the power to the pavement is a set of 20-inch alloys wrapped in low-profile rubber that looks to have plenty of tread left.

In the RS2, Roush left the drivetrain untouched. That's okay, though, since this model year's GT sported Ford's mad-modular Coyote 5.0 V8, an engine that, despite being naturally aspirated, makes a stout 412 horsepower and 390 pound-feet of torque. That's properly routed through a six-speed manual and, according to the seller, a one-piece driveshaft installed by a previous owner feeding the limited-slip rear end. This was the last Mustang to offer the comforting simplicity of a live rear axle.

The previous owner also installed a short-shift kit and long-tube headers. The seller avers that the car is "very fun to drive" and has been "well cared for." Currently, it has 41,000 miles on the clock and comes with a clean title. It's well known that Mustang GTs enjoy a reputation for car event exit shenanigans that often end with an introduction to a curb, tree, or unsuspecting bystander. It would be a shame to let his car's clean presentation meet that fate.

raw_summary: The LN4 Fusion team co-founded by Formula 1 champion Lando Norris has succeeded in getting on the Formula 2 grid as early as 2027. F1's main feeder series F2 has named LN4 Fusion as one of 11 teams selected for the 2027-29 cycle of the championship.

article_paragraphs: The LN4 Fusion team co-founded by Formula 1 champion Lando Norris has succeeded in getting on the Formula 2 grid as early as 2027.
F1's main feeder series F2 has named LN4 Fusion as one of 11 teams selected for the 2027-29 cycle of the championship.

It will compete against 10 established F2 teams, having taken over the entry slot that belonged to race-winning squad AIX Racing (which had sold selected assets to LN4 Fusion and had already handed over its Formula 3 entry slot to the new project).

Formula Regional graduates Dion Gowda and Gabriel Gomez and Eurocup-3 champion James Egozi (driving for IndyCar star Alex Palou's team) have already been announced as the all-rookie F3 line-up for the new team, but it is not yet known who will drive for the project in F2.

But its entry to the grid marks the F2 return of ex-Prema luminaries Rene Rosin and Guillaume Capietto, who oversaw successful F2 title campaigns for the likes of Charles Leclerc, Mick Schumacher and Oscar Piastri (as well as a Pierre Gasly title in the last season before GP2 was renamed F2).
The three-year F2 cycle that begins in 2027 will feature a revised car , styled to reflect the latest set of F1 chassis regulations.

A middling start, radio communication problems that were labelled a "disaster", and annoyance over the strategy had, however, nothing to do with his future engineer Tom Hart being at his side for the first time.

article_paragraphs: Max Verstappen's first step towards life away from long-serving Formula 1 race engineer Gianpiero Lambiase was not straightforward, thanks to a messy United States Grand Prix.

A middling start, radio communication problems that were labelled a "disaster", and annoyance over the strategy had, however, nothing to do with his future engineer Tom Hart being at his side for the first time.
As part of Red Bull's preparations to phase Lambiase out ahead of his switch to McLaren, by 2028 at the latest, the team has begun handing his replacement Hart more responsibilities.
Hart had already filled in during a few practice sessions since the summer break and at Austin he stepped up for the entire weekend, with Lambiase keeping a watching brief in the background.

It was not an easy weekend, especially because of the radio problems that the team remains baffled by, but Red Bull was upbeat about how things went considering it was Hart and Verstappen's first race together.

Team principal Laurent Mekies said: "I think he [Hart] did an excellent job, and you see me smiling because I certainly remember what it is to be on your first race as a race engineer - and he picked a fairly complicated race to do that."

Red Bull knows that a strong dynamic between driver and engineer cannot be built overnight, so even though Hart and Verstappen know each other very well it is going to take time for them to reach the level of understanding that Verstappen has enjoyed with Lambiase.
Mekies said that his impression over the weekend was that the dynamic had bedded down as well as could be expected.

raw_title: The unusual Aston Martin, Honda and Red Bull Powertrains rumours put into perspective
title: The unusual Aston Martin, Honda and Red Bull Powertrains rumours put into perspective
raw_summary: One of the most remarkable moments on Sunday in Austin did not take place on the track itself, but rather in the Formula 1 paddock after the US Grand Prix. During the usual post-race media sessions, both Aston Martin and Red Bull’s representatives were asked about a subject that had very little to do with the race at the Circuit of the Americas – quite the opposite, in fact. Both Aston Martin's chief trackside officer Mike Krack and Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies were asked whether they could rule out a potential partnership between the two brands in the future. It seems rather extraordinary, and both men understandably looked surprised when that question randomly came up during their media rounds, which is why the matter requires some context.

article_paragraphs: One of the most remarkable moments on Sunday in Austin did not take place on the track itself, but rather in the Formula 1 paddock after the US Grand Prix. During the usual post-race media sessions, both Aston Martin and Red Bull’s representatives were asked about a subject that had very little to do with the race at the Circuit of the Americas – quite the opposite, in fact.

Both Aston Martin's chief trackside officer Mike Krack and Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies were asked whether they could rule out a potential partnership between the two brands in the future. It seems rather extraordinary, and both men understandably looked surprised when that question randomly came up during their media rounds, which is why the matter requires some context.

It all goes back to a BBC article and a somewhat unfortunate interpretation of it. In the regular Q&A column of F1 correspondent Andrew Benson, he was asked whether customer teams might be interested in the Red Bull Ford power unit, given that it appears to be more than competitive in its first year.

The answer made it abundantly clear that no F1 team is currently looking for a power unit and then rightly highlighted something that is widely known in the paddock: the shock at Aston Martin, particularly for team owner Lawrence Stroll, when it became apparent earlier this year just how far behind Honda was on the power unit side at the start of F1’s new era.

That understandably led to some initial doubts and considerations, although the decision was made to remain fully committed to Honda – something the BBC article also correctly emphasised. The only speculative element that left the door slightly open was the possibility that those doubts could resurface if Honda fails to make the expected step forward in, let’s say, 2027 or 2028.

As so often happens in F1 and today's media landscape, the story subsequently took on a life of its own and became a bigger talking point than it should have been, according to several insiders. It is a self-fulfilling prophecy: something automatically becomes a topic, rightly or wrongly, if enough people in the F1 paddock are asked about it, which in turn generates coverage. It is a snowball effect, making it crucial to put such stories into perspective.

Both Krack and Mekies were asked on Sunday evening whether they could deny that talks were taking place between Aston Martin and Red Bull Powertrains, with the implication of that question naturally going considerably further than anything suggested in the original BBC article. Krack was quick to reaffirm Aston Martin's long-term commitment to Honda.

“I can only say we have a long-term partner, which is Honda, that by the way has done its 500th race this weekend. And I think we will be together also when we win our first race together”, the Aston Martin representative said.

title: FIA announces new partnership to help drive future F1 regulations
raw_summary: The FIA has announced a wide-ranging partnership with Amazon Web Services as it aims to upgrade its digital capabilities. AWS will join as its Official AI and Cloud Computing Partner, as the governing body will use AWS's suite of AI tools to improve its capability to produce future technical regulations.
summary: The FIA has announced a wide-ranging partnership with Amazon Web Services as it aims to upgrade its digital capabilities. AWS will join as its Official AI and Cloud Computing Partner, as the governing body will use AWS's suite of AI tools to improve its capability to produce future technical regulations.
article_paragraphs: The FIA has announced a wide-ranging partnership with Amazon Web Services as it aims to upgrade its digital capabilities.
AWS will join as its Official AI and Cloud Computing Partner, as the governing body will use AWS's suite of AI tools to improve its capability to produce future technical regulations.

The FIA also runs its aerodynamic simulations on AWS’s High Performance Computing technology, allowing it to conduct air flow tests in the virtual world without having to build physical parts, speeding up the process and reducing the costs involved.

This partnership also expands the digital licensing platform the governing body uses to simplify tasks like licence administration, which should make it easier for national sporting authorities to run their events and for officials to sign up. That digital platform, first trialled in Canada and Sri Lanka, will now be rolled out across more countries.

The AWS integration forms part of the FIA’s wider digital transformation, as president Mohammed Ben Sulayem explained. "Technology is changing every part of our sport, and the FIA must lead that change. Our new partnership with AWS will support everything from the cars of the future to the grassroots clubs where so many careers begin.

"By bringing world-class cloud and AI technology into the heart of the FIA, we can make it simpler for drivers, officials and volunteers to take part, help our Member Clubs work more efficiently, and move closer to our ambition of doubling global motor sport participation."

AWS is already an existing partner of F1 management, having joined in 2018 as its innovation technology partner. Among other services, AWS tools process telemetry data for broadcast use, powering live strategy predictions.

title: Bosch’s popular e-bike motor just got upgraded with more power and less weight

The new motor is designed primarily for everyday riders, including commuters, recreational cyclists, and those who want a comfortable e-bike that can handle everything from city streets to weekend trail rides.

article_paragraphs: Bosch has unveiled the latest generation of its popular Active Line Plus electric bicycle motor, bringing more power, less weight, and a significantly smaller footprint to one of the company’s most widely used drive systems.

The new motor is designed primarily for everyday riders, including commuters, recreational cyclists, and those who want a comfortable e-bike that can handle everything from city streets to weekend trail rides.
And while it isn’t Bosch’s most powerful motor, the upgrades are fairly substantial.

The new Active Line Plus now produces up to 600 watts of peak power and 60 Nm of torque, along with a maximum pedal assistance level of 340%. That’s enough to give riders a healthy boost when accelerating away from traffic lights or climbing hills, without necessarily turning their everyday commuter into an overpowered mountain bike.
Like its predecessor, the motor is designed for Class 1 electric bicycles in the US, providing pedal assistance up to 20 mph (32 km/h) without a throttle.

Remember, the Active Line motor is the drive system model that many e-bike companies use for their modestly performing e-bikes . It gives good power and control, combined with all the tech we’ve come to expect from Bosch, but it isn’t the motor e-bike makers use when they need an electric mountain bike to scale a steep mountainous trail.
Perhaps even more interesting than the increased power is what Bosch has done to the motor’s physical design.
The company developed a new two-stage gearbox that helps reduce the motor’s overall volume by 17% while shaving approximately 1.1 lb (0.5 kg) off its weight.

When ebikes moved into the mass market, Pedego was slow to adapt, and as a result, its $4,000 ebikes felt expensive and uncompetitive . Its retail stores were compelling and it felt like the company had a solid foothold in the market, so we were excited when Pedego reached out about the more affordable $2,195 Pedego Element 2.
Disclaimer: Pedego provided the Element 2 to the author for the purposes of this review.

We were excited to put the model through its paces to see how the company had improved its bikes for the masses and to see if they had cut any corners to achieve the lower pricing that they’re now able to offer. Assembly for the Pedego Element 2 was straightforward. It needed pedals, the handlebars to be mounted to the stem, and a few other odds and ends. But all told, it was very easy and straightforward to get it from the box to being street ready.

Hitting the streets, we found the low-step frame to be extremely comfortable, with an attractive colorway in its satin finish paint. Ours came in a sand color that’s extremely attractive and looks modern with the black accents on the bike.

The Element 2 has an integrated rack to which Pedego fitted a set of panniers for us that make it just the ultimate cargo bike right out of the box. We loaded this up with some groceries on a neighborhood run to pick up some food for dinner and found it to be more than capable of both getting down the hill loaded up with groceries and, obviously back to the house.

Taking it on a run down to the beach, the Pedego is a breeze and feels very confident, especially with its oversized knobby tires. Their larger volume gives it a bit of extra cushion and complements the front suspension fork, making for a very comfortable and confident ride whether you’re on the road or on a short bit of dirt.

On that note, don’t let the knobby tires and suspension fork fool you into thinking this is an all-terrain machine. While it can handle the occasional stint on the dirt, it was never designed to excel in off-road adventures.

title: A Rare 1993 Panoz Roadster V8 – An American-Made Caterham Killer
raw_summary: This is a 1993 Panoz Roadster, and amazingly, it has just 695 miles on the odometer since it was new. One of the reasons for this is that this car was built for company founder Dan Panoz as his personal car, it was then largely used for PR and promotional duties. The Panoz Roadster was one of the most unusual, and capable, low-volume sports cars in production in the United States in the mid-1990s. The Panoz Roadster was one of the most unusual, and capable, low-volume sports cars in production in the United States in the mid-1990s. It had a chassis designed by Frank Costin, a body designed by former Porsche stylist Freeman Thomas, and it had the kind of sharp, intuitive handling of cars like the Caterham 7 .

Panoz Auto Development only built 44 examples of its original Roadster between 1992 and 1995, and 176 of the aluminum-framed “AIV Roadster” that replaced it. Both used Ford Mustang running gear, and unusually, the model line began when Dan Panoz bought the rights to an Irish sports car whose manufacturer was going into receivership.
Panoz Auto Development only built 44 examples of its original Roadster between 1992 and 1995, and 176 of the aluminum-framed “AIV Roadster” that replaced it. Image courtesy of Panoz Auto Development.

Dan Panoz founded his namesake company in 1989 with backing from his father, Don, who’d made his fortune in pharmaceuticals and drug delivery, including the wildly successful transdermal nicotine patch for those wanting to quit smoking.

In 1988, Dan approached the Thompson Manufacturing Company of Wexford, which had been building the TMC Costin since 1983. The Costin was a sports car, essentially a Lotus Seven rival, with a chassis designed by legendary British engineer Frank Costin.

TMC was going into receivership, so Dan bought the rights and shipped its jigs, drawings and two sets of parts to Georgia. His first workshop was a former state salt shed. Two TMC men came too. The engineer soon flew home, unhappy that the car’s original 1.6 liter engine was to make way for a Ford V8, but the head fabricator Mick Murphy stayed on long-term.

Dan wanted the reliability that most small-volume sports cars lacked, so he used a complete Mustang driveline – including the engine, clutch, cooling system, Borg-Warner T-5 five-speed, as well as the rear axle and brakes. The company says a shortened driveshaft and the fuel tank were the only non-Ford parts needed to install it.

article_paragraphs: A hybrid Toyota minivan is easily one of the most rational vehicles you could get , but the automaker has issued a recall on its current model that puts a fly in that perfect-family-car ointment. According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration report on a recall submitted last Tuesday, Toyota is recalling 228,367 Siennas from model years 2022 to 2026, built from September 16, 2021 through July 20 of this year. The current, hybrid-only version of the Sienna came on the scene for the 2021 model year, so it looks like those first model year cars aren't affected.

Per the report, the issue has to do with "certain recliner assemblies by a certain supplier during a certain production period equipped with a seat containing a certain seat belt pretensioner by a certain supplier." That's a direct quote from the NHTSA report, by the way.

Look, I know it's a serious safety issue and I'm sure that passage was vetted by many, many Toyota lawyers, but it's always funny to read official legal stuff like that written with the same tone as that one friend dishing gossip at brunch with feigned discretion after one too many mimosas.

The defect has to do with current-gen Siennas equipped with two captain's chairs in the middle row (read: seven-passenger models). These seats can recline and have seat belts that tighten in the event of a crash. Toyota discovered that in certain frontal collisions, the load produced by the seat belt pretensioner can cause "oscillation" in the recliner mechanism, in turn causing the seat backs to potentially move around during the crash. No bueno for occupant safety.

Toyota apparently discovered the flaw last year when it was doing prototype sled testing for a new second-row seat and seat belt design for a future vehicle, and has since been doing additional tests, even recovering second-row seat assemblies from the field to see how recliner mechanisms have held up over time in the real world. The report goes on to say that Toyota does not have a real estimate as to how many of the 228,000 or so Siennas involved actually have the defect (the "1%" reported at the top of the report is essentially a placeholder). According to the company, there have been no Field Technical Reports or warranty claims related to this defect.

As a no-charge fix, "the majority of involved vehicles" will get an updated version of the software that controls the seat belt pretensioner. About 200 Siennas equipped with the Mobility as a Service Package, meanwhile, will get new seat backs with a different recliner mechanism.

article_paragraphs: HARTFORD, Connecticut — Today, Sierra Club Connecticut, local environmental justice leaders, the Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America, and state elected officials hosted a Press Conference on Connecticut’s High Asthma Rates in the Legislative Office Building.

Hartford ranked eighth in the Asthma and Allergy Foundation’s rankings of “ Asthma Capitals ” due to the city’s higher asthma rates and related deaths. Pollution from fossil fuel plants and systems, like the Capitol Area System, are heavy contributors to poor air quality and asthma risk in Connecticut.

A former co-generation power plant purchased by the State of Connecticut in 2022, the Capitol Area System requires extensive repair in order to continue providing heating and cooling to state and private buildings along its two mile loop, including the Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP) and the Appellate Court.

The Capitol Area System currently runs on methane gas to heat and cool the over a dozen buildings. Sierra Club is urging the State of Connecticut to lead by example and commit to a fossil fuel free, 100 percent renewable solution.

“It is beyond upsetting to see Hartford once again reach the near top of the Asthma Capitals list,” said Alycia Jenkins, Sierra Club Connecticut Organizer . “For generations, we have seen first hand here in our city how poor air quality is making our children, elders, and neighbors sicker. Now is the time for Connecticut to correct course and better address the air pollution from power plants and vehicles that is poisoning our air and worsening public health.”

“Clean air is not a luxury. It is essential to our health,” said Sen. Saud Anwar, a practicing pulmonary physician. “Air pollution puts us all at risk, but especially our children, seniors and people living with asthma. We know the harm, and we have the tools to do better. It is time to act.”

“This is a wakeup call for Connecticut policymakers and advocates. We need to do more to adopt asthma protective policies, especially in our urban communities,” said Dr. Mark Mitchell, environmental and public health physician .

“Policy makers have the power to make changes to save and improve lives and reduce asthma-related costs to society,” said Silva Sedrakian, Executive Director of Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America, New England Chapter .

title: Central Heat Pump Water Heaters Are On The Up & Up
raw_summary: Central heat pump water heaters (HPWH) are on the up and up by any way you measure it. These HPWHs heat water for bigger buildings such as apartment complexes, hotels, and grocery stores. More manufacturers are getting into the market and producing a variety of products. More innovations are helping drive down costs and are making these efficient water heaters a better fit for any application or building. On the first day of Heat Pump Water Heater Week , we devoted most of the sessions to updates on central HPWHs and heard lots of exciting developments. I’m live-blogging updates on all the great content from the week and here are some highlights from the sessions devoted to efficient central water heating.

article_paragraphs: Central heat pump water heaters (HPWH) are on the up and up by any way you measure it. On the first day of Heat Pump Water Heater Week , we devoted most of the sessions to updates on central HPWHs and heard lots of exciting developments. I’m live-blogging updates on all the great content from the week and here are some highlights from the sessions devoted to efficient central water heating.

We first got an update on packaged central heat pump water heating systems. These are systems that are built offsite with heat pumps, piping, storage, and swing tanks all constructed and tested in a laboratory before being delivered to a building.

Albert Rooks from Water Drop walked us through exactly how a skid-mounted CHPWH is built and delivered and how easy it can be to plug it into a building, no assembly required. Madison Johnson from Ecotope then walked through a case study of how packaged central HPWHs operate in the real world. Key to success, according to Madison, is making sure temperatures on swing tanks aren’t too high, which can really reduce efficiency (since they use electric resistance). Jake Bucklin from Lync also joined the conversation and discussed specific HPWH systems. These systems resemble packaged central HPWHs in that they are designed and built by one manufacturer but differ in that they are shipped in pieces and assembled on site. Specified systems can be better options for retrofits, which might have more space limitations.

From packaged systems, the conversation then turned to how to handle upfront costs of both residential and commercial HPWHs, which can be a major barrier, even if HPWHs save lots of money on utility bills and pay for themselves (which they almost always do).

Gregg Holladay and Kevin Clark from Bradford White discussed on-bill financing for heat pump water heaters. They encouraged utilities to set up programs to provide low- or no-cost financing for homeowners switching to HPWHs as a way to help drive the product and increase efficiency in their territory.

Then, Machias Schoen from Palmetto talked about HPWH leasing. Leasing a HPWH rather than owning it can both help with the upfront cost barrier (leases are usually zero money down) and include monitoring and maintenance which will ensure systems continue to perform well.

Finally, Andy McNamara from Carbon Zero Buildings talked about their innovative way of both braiding incentives and having contractors finance construction costs to enable building owners to install central HPWHs at low or no cost. Seems like an effective approach, and the Carbon Zero Buildings team has been installing central HPWH systems like hotcakes in California.

A Mercedes-AMG-sourced twin-turbo V-8 acts as the base of the Valhalla's ultra-powerful plug-in hybrid powertrain, aided by two electric motors in the front and one integrated into the eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. Torque-vectoring all-wheel drive and active aerodynamics in the front and rear help the Valhalla stick like flypaper. It might sound like you need an FIA Super License to get the most out of Aston's road-legal racecar, but that's where the Valhalla's magic truly lies—it's approachable enough to make even novices feel godlike at the racetrack.

Good news for those looking for a ride that can hit 217 mph with the top down: Aston Martin is adding a new Spider variant to the Valhalla lineup for the 2028 model year. The Valhalla Spider comes with a removable fabric soft-top roof as standard. With the fabric roof in place, the Valhalla's top speed is limited to a mere 124 mph. Customers in the U.S. also get a carbon fiber hard-top roof, which unlocks the Aston's full 217-mph Vmax.

raw_summary: For the billionaire who has always wondered what it's like to feel the wind rushing through their new hair plugs at 217 mph, Aston Martin has announced a new topless version of its utterly bonkers Valhalla supercar, the Valhalla Spider . It'll debut at the 2026 Concours at Wynn Las Vegas, and despite the name, rich arachnophobes can rest easy knowing the Valhalla Spider comes with a black fabric roof in most markets, or an optional carbon fiber hard top that's standard on U.S. market cars to keep the elements out when necessary. article_paragraphs: For the billionaire who has always wondered what it's like to feel the wind rushing through their new hair plugs at 217 mph, Aston Martin has announced a new topless version of its utterly bonkers Valhalla supercar, the Valhalla Spider . It'll debut at the 2026 Concours at Wynn Las Vegas, and despite the name, rich arachnophobes can rest easy knowing the Valhalla Spider comes with a black fabric roof in most markets, or an optional carbon fiber hard top that's standard on U.S. market cars to keep the elements out when necessary.

The Valhalla Spider is powered by the same twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter flat-plane crank V8 paired with a plug-in hybrid system, all of which produces a combined output of 1,064 horsepower and 811 pound-feet of torque — the same as the Valhalla coupe. The Spider also gets two front axle-mounted motors and one motor integrated into the 8-speed dual-clutch transmission, with no mechanical connection between the front and rear axles.

Differences between the Spider and the coupe include a taller intake snorkel, a clip-in wind deflector that stores in the sills, and a revised electronic stability program and active aero to handle roof-on or roof-off 200-mph+ runs. With the standard fabric top fitted, though, its top speed is limited to a rather pedestrian 124 mph. To go faster, you'll need to go topless or opt for that carbon roof.

Going topless hasn't forced Aston to drop the Valhalla's dihedral doors. In fact, chopping the top made getting in and out a bit easier — and not just when the top is removed. According to Aston Martin, "Valhalla Spider retains its signature carbon fiber dihedral doors, preserving the sense of theater; now with refined kinematics for smoother operation and a transition to a frameless design. A small increase in the curvature of the door glass top edge also improves entry and exit when the roof is fitted."

A new carbon fiber Touring Seat comes standard on the Valhalla Spider, which is also meant to enhance ease of entry and exit with the roof on, though the original carbon fiber seat form the Valhalla Coupe can be optioned at no extra cost for better support.

Despite losing its roof, the Valhalla Spider still uses a version of the coupe's bespoke carbon fiber tub designed and engineered by Aston Martin Performance Technologies, the consulting arm of the company's F1 team. The Valhalla Coupe was priced around $1 million when it debuted in 2024, but considering the giant leap in inflation and the naturally pricier nature of convertibles, this one will likely be much more. And if you have to ask about the Valhalla Spider's price tag, you absolutely cannot afford one.

raw_summary: Over the coming year, renewables’ share of total generating capacity will grow from 37.7% to 40.4%, surpassing that of natural gas and outstripping nuclear capacity fivefold, according to new data released by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) and reviewed by the SUN DAY Campaign. article_paragraphs: Over the coming year, renewables’ share of total generating capacity will grow from 37.7% to 40.4%, surpassing that of natural gas and outstripping nuclear capacity fivefold, according to new data released by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) and reviewed by the SUN DAY Campaign.

According to the EIA’s latest “ Electric Power Monthly ” report (with data through August 31, 2026), renewably generated electricity during the first two-thirds of 2026 was 10.2% greater year over year. The growth was led by utility-scale [>1 MW] solar (up 20.0%), small-scale solar (up 12.0%), wind (up 7.8%), hydropower (up 4.2%), and geothermal (up 3.8%).

From January to August 2026, wind produced 333,367 gigawatt-hours (GWh) – 10.6% of total US electrical generation – while utility-scale and small-scale solar combined produced 329,119 GWh (10.5%), hydropower produced 180,940 GWh (5.7%), biomass produced 29,917 GWh (1.0%), and geothermal produced 10,766 GWh (0.34%).
By comparison, the electrical output of US natural gas and nuclear power plants grew more slowly – by just 2.6% and 1.3%, respectively. Electricity produced by US coal plants fell by 8.7%.

During the first eight months of 2026, the combination of wind and solar, including small-scale solar, accounted for almost 21.1% of domestic electricity production, with wind at 10.6% and solar at nearly 10.5%.
During the first two-thirds of this year, wind and solar combined produced 44.4% more electricity than coal and 24.8% more than nuclear.
Through the end of August, the mix of all renewables, including biomass, accounted for 28.1% of total US electrical generation – up from 26.2% a year earlier.

Between September 1, 2025, and August 31, 2026, the installed capacity of utility-scale solar increased by 27,141.7 MW, while that of small-scale solar and wind grew by 6,526.1 MW and 9,979.1 MW (including 800 MW of offshore wind), respectively. The combined capacity of all renewable energy sources, including hydropower, biomass, and geothermal, expanded by 43,497.9 MW.

raw_summary: If you want a motorcycle that does everything, you buy a BMW GS . It's such an easy choice, so rote that even BMW itself has felt the need to specialize its adventure lineup away from such perfectly omnicapable bikes. article_paragraphs: If you want a motorcycle that does everything, you buy a BMW GS . It's such an easy choice, so rote that even BMW itself has felt the need to specialize its adventure lineup away from such perfectly omnicapable bikes. Now, though, another brand thinks it can hit the Bavarians where their hold is strongest. Triumph has revamped the Tiger 1200 lineup to hit BMW where it hurts, and the Brits have a solid shot of making a real mark.

The Tiger 1200 line is still split into its four component models — GT Pro, Rally Pro, GT Explorer, and Rally Explorer — but Triumph has streamlined things between the four bikes to make their differences clearer. Every model now comes with a 19 inch front wheel and a 17 out back, and all four get trick self-lowering Showa suspension with 7.9 inches of travel front and rear — until you come to a stop, at which point the system drops the bike almost 1.2 inches.

Triumph says the seat height, with a low seat installed and the self-lowering suspension active, can get as low as 31.1 inches at a stop. That's impressively low for a big adventure bike, and over an inch shorter than the competing R 1300 GS. On top of the trick suspension updates, Triumph has updated the Tiger's rider display — a new 7-inch display with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto now standard. There's also the updated 1,160cc three-cylinder engine with a redesigned cylinder head, new pistons, lighter intake and exhaust valves, and revised gear ratios for first, second, and third. The engine now makes 155.8 horsepower (up from 147 hp). Triumph also claims that the new Tiger 1200 has more torque down low, which improves slow-speed performance.

If you're a bit confused by all the Tiger 1200's available variants, here's how Triumph differentiates them: GT bikes get cast wheels, while the Rally bikes get spokes. Rally bikes get an extra off-road ride mode and some engine protection. Explorer bikes get wider and taller handlebars and 7.9-gallon fuel tanks rather than the Pro bikes' 5.3-gallon units. Got all that?

Essentially, they're the same chassis, engine, and suspension across all models, but the Rally bikes get some dirt features, and Explorer bikes get the right gear for long tours . All four get Bosch radar front and rear, as well, to enable both adaptive cruise control and rear close-follow warnings — they're all competent tourers, big tank or no.

The best change for 2027 to my eye, though, is the appearance of the new Tiger 1200 lineup. The prior bikes were stuck in an awkward in-between period, where Triumph was in the process of ditching its long-lasting twin-headlight design but hadn't yet gone all-in on compact LED illumination. Now it has, and the Tiger looks all the better for it — that single center headlight below the light bar really works for me. It's functional, too, with corner lighting built into the central LED that illuminates when the rider leans.

raw_title: GM is embracing hybrids now
title: GM is embracing hybrids now
raw_summary: General Motors plans to invest in its Lansing Delta Township Assembly plant to handle future production of hybrid-electric vehicles, the latest move by the U.S. automaker to claw back market share by appealing to the shifting tastes of consumers. The company said on Tuesday that it plans to invest more than $2 billion over the next several years in the broader Lansing region, an amount that includes $1.25 billion to prepare the assembly plant for “future vehicle production.”
summary: General Motors plans to invest in its Lansing Delta Township Assembly plant to handle future production of hybrid-electric vehicles, the latest move by the U.S. automaker to claw back market share by appealing to the shifting tastes of consumers. The company said on Tuesday that it plans to invest more than $2 billion over the next several years in the broader Lansing region, an amount that includes $1.25 billion to prepare the assembly plant for “future vehicle production.”
article_paragraphs: General Motors plans to invest in its Lansing Delta Township Assembly plant to handle future production of hybrid-electric vehicles, the latest move by the U.S. automaker to claw back market share by appealing to the shifting tastes of consumers.

The company said on Tuesday that it plans to invest more than $2 billion over the next several years in the broader Lansing region, an amount that includes $1.25 billion to prepare the assembly plant for “future vehicle production.”

The company said it is working with the U.S. Department of Energy to restructure a previously awarded Domestic Manufacturing Conversion Grant and direct those funds to future hybrid production at the Lansing factory. The company was awarded $500 million under the Biden administration to support converting a different factory in Lansing to produce electric vehicles, including hybrid, battery-electric, plug-in electric hybrid, and hydrogen fuel cell electric vehicles. Those funds were never released, according to GM.
Today, GM assembles the gas-powered Buick Enclave, Chevrolet Traverse, and GMC Acadia at the Lansing Delta Township factory, which produced a record 291,000 vehicles in 2025.

GM didn’t provide specifics on when it would begin producing and selling hybrid vehicles. But insiders told TechCrunch to expect hybrids across multiple brands rather than a single vehicle line. A Reuters report , citing anonymous sources, said the company plans to build hybrid versions of the Chevrolet Traverse, Buick Enclave, and GMC Acadia at the factory.

Hybrids have become increasingly popular, thanks in part to rising gas prices. Customers also have more choices than ever before, with most automakers offering a range of hybrid and plug-in hybrid models. Toyota is the U.S. market leader in hybrid sales, followed by Honda. Ford has also gained considerable market share in hybrid sales in the past two years, selling some 228,000 hybrids in 2025.

But GM has been slow to adopt hybrids. Until recently, the company’s only electric-hybrid vehicle was the Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray , which launched as a 2024 model. (GM sold 2,444 of those vehicles last year.) The E-Ray has since been discontinued; GM began deliveries of the hybrid Corvette ZR1X in March and next year will launch a hybrid Corvette Grand Sport X.

GM eschewed hybrids in favor of battery-electric vehicles. The automaker invested billions of dollars to shift its gas-powered portfolio to an all-electric one. That strategy has changed under the Trump administration with the end of the federal EV tax credit and slower-than-expected demand. GM hasn’t abandoned EVs completely, though it has seen EV sales fall year-over-year. The company still sells numerous battery-electric vehicles across its brands, including the Chevrolet Equinox EV, Blazer EV, and Cadillac Escalade IQ.

article_paragraphs: Re:Build, the Massachusetts-based manufacturing accelerator that spun out EV startup Slate Auto in 2023, has raised $2.1 billion

The company said Tuesday that it will use the funding to “expand Re:Build’s capacity to manufacture hard tech products and launch new industrial startups,” which will “ensure the most innovative products can be made in America for generations to come.” The investment was led by General Catalyst and JPMorganChase’s Strategic Investment Group. Other investors weren’t disclosed.
The funding round comes as increasing attention and capital is flowing to the idea of building up manufacturing and supply chains in the United States, especially as a hedge away from China.

“We started Re:Build because the deindustrialization of America is an economic failure and national security risk,” Re:Build co-founder Jeff Wilke said in a statement. “This capital allows Re:Build to go faster and further than would otherwise be possible, and build a great manufacturing business and a platform for American industrial leadership. The products and companies emerging from our ecosystem prove we can help restore America’s industrial might.”

General Catalyst’s CEO Hemant Taneja echoed those sentiments in a statement, saying, “General Catalyst has long believed that rebuilding American industrial capacity is one of the most important economic and national security imperatives of our time.”

Taneja added: “To compete with China, re-industrialize the U.S., and revitalize the towns and jobs that have been left behind, we need platform companies that can operate at genuine scale — and we need our innovation ecosystem to learn how to build hardware again.”

Founded in 2020, Re:Build bills itself as “America’s answer to Shenzhen,” and it has numerous ties to Amazon. It was co-founded by Wilke, who was Amazon’s former commercial CEO. Wei Gao, a longtime Amazon VP and technical adviser to Bezos, is Re:Build’s chief digital and product officer. Multiple other Re:Build executives also worked for the e-commerce giant.

Re:Build claims to have “launched hundreds of products and production systems” over its six-year existence. The company tends to operate two ways: It enters partnerships with industrial companies to “design, engineer, and manufacture products at scale across verticals including aerospace and defense,” and it incubates startups in “critical, underserved markets.”

article_paragraphs: Volkswagen’s latest recall now extends to Audi, affecting more than 9,000 Q4 E-Tron and Q4 Sportback E-Tron vehicles. And just like with the ID.4, owners are being told to limit charging to 80% of the battery’s capacity.
Earlier this month, Volkswagen issued a recall impacting 22,524 ID.4 electric SUVs, model years 2023 to 2026.
The recall is due to the risk of thermal propagation, or a battery fire, under certain conditions when charged to over 80% of its limit.

Volkswagen said in a safety recall report with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) that “certain charging profiles combined with a state of charge over 80% may trigger thermal propagation.”

While the root cause is unknown, Volkswagen urged owners to limit charging to 80%. Owners of affected vehicles received an email saying VW “intends to apply a temporary vehicle setting that limits charging to 80%,” unless they opted out by October 21.
In the letter sent to the NHTSA on October 23, Volkswagen Group of America said it was issuing a recall affecting 9,048 Audi Q4 E-Tron and Q4 Sportback E-Tron vehicles model years 2024 to 2025.
The safety recall follows Audi’s Product Safety Committee being informed of battery thermal events involving other Volkswagen Group EVs that use the same batteries as the Audi Q4 E-Tron.

Following an internal investigation, Audi found the same battery and production characteristics as the impacted VW Group vehicles. Audi said the majority of these were produced for the North American market.

article_paragraphs: The Ford Motor Company is still disguising the soon-to-arrive Fathom electric pickup truck under a layer of camouflage, but the iconic automaker is more than happy to share what’s going on inside. In the latest news drop, Ford wants everyone to know that you don’t need an expensive inverter to convert the truck into a mobile, zero emission generating station for your home.

The idea of using an EV battery to power household appliances seemed pretty futuristic back in the early 2010’s, but nowadays the technology is commonplace. The key is bidirectional charging technology, which enables an EV battery to discharge electricity as well as receive it from a charging station.

One obvious use is backup emergency power, where EV batteries have the advantage of quiet, pollution-free running — unlike gas or diesel generators. In case of a prolonged power outage, drivers can travel outside of the blackout area, charge up, and return with a fully charged battery to keep the lights on at home.

EV batteries can also help ratepayers avoid higher peak demand electricity rates. Households with home EV charging stations can time their charging sessions to take advantage of utility discounts for off-peak use, and discharge their battery to avoid high rates during peak periods.

The sticky wicket, of course, is cost. Generally speaking, home EV charging stations are not free, and neither is the inverter needed to convert the DC current from an EV battery into an AC current for household use.

Ford’s answer is a built-in system that eliminates the need for an external inverter. “Our goal wasn’t just to add bidirectional power to our EVs. It was to redesign the system to cost far less so more people can access bidirectional power ,” Ford Model e general manager Kay Hart explained in a new post earlier today.
“With Fathom offering bidirectional power at an MSRP starting below $30,000, even more people can benefit from potential energy savings and home backup power,” Hart added.
That seems to suggest that the cost is included in the company’s target MSRP of $28,350, though in another part of the post Hart uses the word “available,” which typically means an add-on:

raw_title: The KTM X-Bow Is Finally Coming To American Roads
title: The KTM X-Bow Is Finally Coming To American Roads
raw_summary: The KTM X-Bow has been around since 2008, but there has never been a road-legal production version available in the United States — until now. KTM X-Bow has just announced the X-Bow GT-XA, a U.S. road version of its nimble sports car. The spun-off Austrian manufacturer plans to build 30 cars for the model's first year of production, but there is just one hiccup. The GT-XA has yet to be approved for U.S. road use. KTM X-Bow stated that its exclusive U.S. partner, Carbon Yard, is working to secure U.S. road legalization for the GT-XA. Regardless of how long that takes, the factory in Graz, Austria, will be assembling sports cars with a delivery target of 2027 in mind. Prospective buyers can place reservations for $50,000, which will remain fully refundable until the GT-XA becomes road legal. KTM X-Bow has yet to announce technical specifications or a final MSRP for the U.S.-spec two-seater, but is anticipating a $490,000 price tag.

KTM X-Bow has just announced the X-Bow GT-XA, a U.S. road version of its nimble sports car. The spun-off Austrian manufacturer plans to build 30 cars for the model's first year of production, but there is just one hiccup. The GT-XA has yet to be approved for U.S. road use.

KTM X-Bow stated that its exclusive U.S. partner, Carbon Yard, is working to secure U.S. road legalization for the GT-XA. Regardless of how long that takes, the factory in Graz, Austria, will be assembling sports cars with a delivery target of 2027 in mind. Prospective buyers can place reservations for $50,000, which will remain fully refundable until the GT-XA becomes road legal. KTM X-Bow has yet to announce technical specifications or a final MSRP for the U.S.-spec two-seater, but is anticipating a $490,000 price tag.

The X-Bow was forever changed when it went racing in 2015. KTM produced a factory racing version for GT4 competition , which necessitated a closed cockpit to fit the regulations. Engineers fitted a canopy over the cockpit because the existing monocoque made doors impractical. The canopy would make its street-legal X-Bow debut in 2022 with the GT-XR, the likely basis for the upcoming GT-XA. According to X-Bow, the U.S.-spec version will feature a front-axle lift system to make it easier to pull into driveways.

The canopy undoubtedly expanded the X-Bow's customer base, but it strayed from the car's initial ethos. The 2,760-pound GT-XR is over 1,000 pounds heavier than the original open-cockpit model. It might not be a true fighter jet canopy, as KTM X-Bow advertises, but I wouldn't want to be inside a canopied X-Bow if it flipped on a public road. I'm not sure I could squeeze my way out of one of those tiny windows. At a race track, at least the marshals are there to respond and help you escape if you end up trapped in an overturned X-Bow.

I don't want to sound too critical of creature comforts, but the original X-Bow was a breath of fresh air for the realm of enthusiast sports cars from a very unusual source. An Austrian motorcycle manufacturer produced a lightweight, open-cockpit sports car constructed around a carbon fiber monocoque. The partnership with dominant single-seat builder Dallara led many to think of the X-Bow as a street-legal, formula-style race car, but its raw agility could easily be described as a four-wheeled motorcycle. The GT-XR just isn't that. I guess I should also mention that, after KTM's massive restructuring , the X-Bow was spun off into a separate company with different owners than the bike maker.

raw_title: This Mid-Engine V8 Geo Metro Is The Ultimate Evolution Of 'LS Swap All The Things'
title: This Mid-Engine V8 Geo Metro Is The Ultimate Evolution Of 'LS Swap All The Things
raw_summary: LS swaps are so common they've become a cliché. We've seen them in everything from Miatas and classic turbocharged Chevy Suburbans to Suzuki kei cars . That means it's perfectly reasonable to drop the big V8 into its Suzuki-made cousin, this Geo Metro currently for sale on Cars & Bids , right? Wait, what do you mean it won't fit in the engine bay where the 1.0-liter inline-3 used to go? That's okay, just rip out the back seats and put it there instead. Of course, it's not nearly that simple. The most obvious visual clue that something's not normal about this car is that the rear quarter panels have been completely rebuilt. The larger wheels, sourced from a Cadillac DeVille, have been pushed beyond the rear corners of the car, giving it an awkward raked appearance. Air scoops have been carved into each side to feed cool air into the rear half of the car, which has been sealed off, hopefully keeping any errant fumes from entering the cabin.

Wait, what do you mean it won't fit in the engine bay where the 1.0-liter inline-3 used to go? That's okay, just rip out the back seats and put it there instead.

Of course, it's not nearly that simple. The most obvious visual clue that something's not normal about this car is that the rear quarter panels have been completely rebuilt. The larger wheels, sourced from a Cadillac DeVille, have been pushed beyond the rear corners of the car, giving it an awkward raked appearance. Air scoops have been carved into each side to feed cool air into the rear half of the car, which has been sealed off, hopefully keeping any errant fumes from entering the cabin.

While the Metro is a small car, the 5.3-liter LS4 V8 somehow fits back here, as well as the four-speed automatic transmission. This version of the LS almost certainly came from a front-wheel-drive sedan of the early 2000s , like the Chevy Impala or Monte Carlo SS, the Pontiac Grand Prix GXP, or even the Buick Lacrosse Super. GM already solved all the packaging problems of a transverse LS before this swap was dreamed up. Then, all the builder had to do was cut, widen, and reinforce the Metro's body to accommodate the existing drivetrain and subframe, as well as to handle its 303 horsepower and 323 pound-feet of torque. The car originally made just 55 hp, so it likely needed all the help it could get.

As part of this build, the cooling system obviously needed to be redesigned, since putting it in front of the engine wouldn't help much in this unique application. A large radiator sits tucked behind the rear bumper, which now looks like a slice of Swiss cheese that allows air to flow through it. Although the car has a recent paint job changing the color to red, the front and rear bumpers remain unpainted, just like the original Metro. There's little original about this LS-swapped Geo (rebadged as a Chevy, like the later Metros were), but somehow that design choice just feels right.

With a V8 stuffed in the rear, the fuel tank needed to move someplace else. The builder took a cue from the VW Beetle, putting the tank in the front of the car where the original engine used to be. This location was good enough for the Porsche 911 , and it's a racing fuel cell, so that must make it at least a little bit safe.

If the Ford Fiesta Shogun is too common for you ( six examples still survive, and you know Jay Leno isn't giving up his), this one-off mid-engine V8 Geo Metro might scratch the same strange itch, and it is currently for sale on Cars & Bids . While it's currently registered in Illinois, the listing does note that, "Due to the modifications performed to this Metro, it may not pass emissions testing in some states." I have a feeling that anyone interested in a V8 Metro is less interested in emissions and fuel economy than in speed and the absolute awesomeness of a build like this.

raw_summary: Buenos Aires, Argentina is separated from Colonia, Uruguay by the Rio de la Plata estuary. While it is possible to drive between the two cities, it is faster and more convenient to take a ferry ride. Buquebus, a popular ferry operator in Buenos Aires, offers round trip excursions to Colonia for a mere $43.00 — a deal if there ever was one. But, wait, it gets better. Today, that journey can take place aboard the China Zorrilla, the world’s largest electric ferry . Don’t let the name fool you; this ship was not manufactured in China. It is named after the popular Uruguayan actress and director Concepción “China” Zorrilla, who is much beloved in both countries. In fact, it was made by Incat in Tasmania, a company that specializes in catamaran style ships. It refers to this vessel simply as Hull 96, which is an aluminum catamaran.

article_paragraphs: Buenos Aires, Argentina is separated from Colonia, Uruguay by the Rio de la Plata estuary. Buquebus, a popular ferry operator in Buenos Aires, offers round trip excursions to Colonia for a mere $43.00 — a deal if there ever was one. But, wait, it gets better. Today, that journey can take place aboard the China Zorrilla, the world’s largest electric ferry .

Don’t let the name fool you; this ship was not manufactured in China. It is named after the popular Uruguayan actress and director Concepción “China” Zorrilla, who is much beloved in both countries. In fact, it was made by Incat in Tasmania, a company that specializes in catamaran style ships. It refers to this vessel simply as Hull 96, which is an aluminum catamaran.

The vessel is 130 meters (426 feet) long and can carry 225 cars and 2100 passengers. Once aboard, those passengers will enjoy all the comforts of a cruise ship, with a variety of dining and shopping opportunities during the approximately one hour long crossing. The ship has a gross tonnage of 14.058 tons and can skim along at 25 knots (29 mph), powered by eight 2400 kW (3200 HP) electric motors that feed eight water jets supplied by Wartsilla . The electricity comes from a 41.2 MWh 250 ton battery pack from Corvus Energy that can be recharged by two 8 MW chargers.

“The water jet propulsion configuration with eight electric motors is the most efficient available on the market today for this speed range and type of application, while also offering all the benefits of Wärtsilä’s axial-flow water jet technology — lightweight, shallow draft, excellent maneuverability, and low maintenance,” said Roger Holm, president for marine power at Wärtsilä.

Incat says the start of operations by China Zorrilla is an important milestone for the electrification of maritime transport. CEO Robert Clifford stated, “This is a truly historic day for Incat, for Tasmania, and for the global maritime industry. Over the years, hundreds of talented people at our shipyard in Hobart have worked tirelessly to make this extraordinary vessel a reality. We have overcome immense technical challenges, pushed the boundaries of what was previously thought possible, and created something the world has never seen before.”

He added the fact that the ferry is now carrying passengers in commercial operation while being fully powered by batteries is an incredible achievement and “a moment of great pride for everyone involved in this journey.”

The China Zorrilla electric ferry demonstrates that even large commercial vessels with high transport capacity can be fully powered by batteries instead of fossil fuels — an important milestone for the shipping industry.

A battery electric vessel will give passengers a quieter crossing that is free from the engine noise, vibration, and stench of exhaust fumes that are typical of diesel propulsion. The fact that the ferry has no direct exhaust emissions of its own while it is in operation is an important bonus.

title: Flock Cameras Are Being Covered With Garbage Bags As Contracts With The Wildly Unpopular Mass Surveillance Company Are Terminated
raw_summary: As the number of cities that have dropped Flock camera contracts has been rising steeply, some of those cities have been unsure how to stop the surveillance that come standard with the now-installed camera hardware. More and more places have resorted to putting trash bags over the cameras, reports WREG News Channel 3 , as a temporary measure to prevent cameras from tracking your every move until they can be removed properly. It's almost like the trash is taking itself out. While some concerned citizens have resorted to vandalism to remove the unwanted cameras, the correct way to make them go away is to work through the proper channels, attend town meetings, and get the communities you live in to decide to take them down themselves. They're much more likely to stay down that way. After all, police continue to misuse this "Big Brother" technology, either by accident or completely on purpose , and Flock customers have been dropping like flies with all the reports of errors and abuses continuing to pop up in the media.
